title: What protection is worth
description: Three numbers bound the price of any maritime escort product: what it costs to avoid the risk entirely (the Cape), what it costs to buy the existing substitute (armed guards), and what the risk itself is priced at (war-risk premium, in risk-economics.json). Anything charged above the cheapest of those is a hard sell.

the_substitute.name: Privately Contracted Armed Security Personnel (PCASP)
the_substitute.vintage_warning: The pricing below is from 2012, at the peak of Somali piracy. It is the clearest published price data available and it establishes the shape of the market, but every figure needs re-basing against a current broker quote before it is used commercially. Treat as historical, not current.

friction: Weapons are legal at sea for self-defence but the law changes the moment the team heads to port. Providers have been arrested and jailed in Somalia, Egypt and Kenya, and some contractors have reportedly dropped weapons overboard before entering weapons-restrictive ports.

Carriage of armed personnel is a flag-state authorisation, with separate legal implications for every coastal and port state on the route. Over 8,000 ports fall under the ISPS Code with no unified rule on armed security.
Some major maritime operators specifically prefer armed escorts precisely because it keeps armed men, and the liability, off their own vessels.
Underwriters give discounts to ships that hire armed guards — which is the mechanism any escort product needs to replicate.

escort_precedent.name: Convoy Escort Programme Ltd
escort_precedent.model: Seven armoured former naval patrol boats, each carrying an eight-man security team, escorting merchant convoys
escort_precedent.price: About $30,000 for one boat escorting a convoy of roughly four commercial vessels for three to four days

derived.ratio: roughly 7-8x cheaper per protected vessel than an embarked armed team
derived.caveat: This is our arithmetic on 2012 figures, not a published finding. It ignores mobilisation, transit positioning, insurance and the fact that convoying forces ships onto a shared schedule.

historic_cost_of_piracy_2012.vintage_warning: 2012 figures at the Somali peak. Useful for orders of magnitude and for showing that the total cost of piracy is borne by many parties at once, not by the shipowner alone.

items.item: Bypassing the Gulf of Aden entirely
items.value: 3,000 extra miles, 2-3 weeks; $3.5 million per year in extra fuel for tankers and $74.4 million per year for the liner trades

items.item: War-risk insurance per ship per voyage
items.value: rose from about $500 in 2007 to about $20,000, excluding injury, liability and ransom cover
$30-150 million in 2008; per vessel from about $500,000 in 2004 to upwards of $5.5 million by 2009

historic_cost_of_piracy_2012.structural_forecast: The Security Association for the Maritime Industry projected in 2012 that over the following twenty years maritime traffic would rise 50% while navies shrank 30%. Fourteen years into that twenty, the Somali resurgence of 2026 is what a widening gap between traffic and naval coverage looks like.

suez_traffic.note: Canal revenue is the cleanest public proxy for whether ships are using the Red Sea. It is Egypt's number, published monthly, and it moves before anything else does.

points.note: Conflicting figure: WorldCargo News reports 2024 at $3.9bn and 2025 at $4.2bn. Both are recorded here rather than one being silently chosen. Verify against the Suez Canal Authority directly before quoting.
Stated by President Sisi in January 2026 as the two-year loss attributed to the Gaza war and the shipping crisis.

recovery_2026.trigger: The Suez Canal Authority attributes recovery to the final quarter of 2025, following the Sharm el-Sheikh summit and the resulting Gaza ceasefire.

imf_projection.note: IMF projection of Suez revenue, showing the expected shape of normalisation.

open_questions: What happened to Convoy Escort Programme Ltd, and why did crewed convoy escort not become standard? This is the single highest-value unanswered question in the library.
What does a PCASP transit cost in 2026, not 2012? Every price in the substitute section needs re-basing from a live broker quote.

Will an underwriter discount a war-risk premium for an autonomous escort, and who certifies it? Armed guards already earn a discount. Without an equivalent, the value has to come entirely from the routing saving.
What is the per-lane, per-ship-class Cape diversion delta after netting off tolls? The headline diversion cost overstates the addressable price, possibly by a lot.
How much would convoying cost a carrier in schedule reliability? Predictability is what carriers say they are buying on the Cape route, and a convoy schedule takes some of it back.
